reading.body:
Power purchase agreements are long-term contracts by which data center operators secure generation, nuclear, solar, wind, or gas, for current and future facilities.

PPAs are described as how the AI-era buildout finances new generation and how operators back their renewable claims, and nuclear agreements specifically, including plant restarts and small modular reactor commitments, are named as the signature deals of this period, a notable detail given how rarely nuclear power has featured in corporate energy purchasing in prior decades. That connects the power purchase agreement metric directly to two other trends tracked elsewhere in this collection, renewable energy utilization claims and the physical constraint of the grid interconnection queue.

It groups with approval to energize versus queued load, capacity market clearing price, and interconnection queue position and wait under Power and grid, the largest sibling cluster in this collection, reflecting how central grid access has become to data center strategy.
